newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bhutto's removal stirs Indonesia palm olein market.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto's removal stirs Indonesia palm olein market.

text.p: Indonesian palm oil traders on Tuesday expressed concern over political developments in Pakistan, fearing the crisis could hit palm oil exports.
"I will be extra cautious when dealing with private Pakistani buyers because problems over payments could arise if there is unrest there," one senior trader said.

Pakistani president Farooq Leghari sacked Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto on Tuesday, accusing her three-year government of corruption and nepotism. Elections were called for February 3 next year. It was the second time Bhutto had been sacked.
Pakistan is a significant importer of palm oil from both Indonesia and Malaysia.
"If for instance there are riots, buyers could declare a force majeure and the situation could become sticky as far as payments are concerned," the trader added.
But some traders said they were not unduly worried, at the moment, over developments in Pakistan.

An Indonesian foreign ministry official, asked to comment on the events in Pakistan, said: "There is no statement regarding that matter." He described relations between Indonesia and Pakistan as "normal".

Pakistani army units took over key installations in Islamabad at about 2 a.m. (2100 GMT Monday) after the order for Bhutto's removal was issued, but there was no sign of any major restriction on movement of traffic in the capital.
The official news agency APP said the president had appointed former parliament speaker Meraj Khalid as interim prime minister.
Indonesian palm olein prices were slightly lower in early trading on Tuesday as buying interest remained scarce.

Traders said olein was around 1,365-70 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,370-75 rupiah at Monday's close. Quotes were also heard at 1,360 rupiah. The traders said a crude palm oil tender expected later today would give the market some direction.
